newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MONACO AND METZ PUT ON THE STYLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO AND METZ PUT ON THE STYLE.

text.p: Monaco and Metz gave the French League plenty to celebrate with stylish wins over Borussia Moenchengladbach and Sporting Lisbon in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday.

Monaco produced the shock result of the night with a 4-2 second round, first leg victory over Moenchengladbach thanks to two goals from Nigerian Victor Ikpeba, and one each from Scot John Collins and Thierry Henry.
The Germans struggled to reproduce the kind of crisp football which destroyed English premier league Arsenal in the last round and now have a hard battle ahead of them in the second leg.
They scored through Christian Hochstaetter and Swede Patrik Andersson.

Moenchengladbach coach Bernd Krauss was fulsome in his praise of Monaco, saying: "We saw what great players the French have. French football is probably ahead of the German game at the moment. I didn't feel we were playing in Europe in the first half. It was more like a friendly."

Monaco coach Jean Tigana, enjoying his first success over a German side as either a player or coach, said: "I am surprised that we have won by as much as we have here. We just wanted to get a goal..."

While Monaco, who were without suspended defender Franck Dumas and the injured Eric Di Meco, Marco Grassi and Enzo Scifo, were ahead of the German game, Metz were certainly ahead of the Portuguese one, scoring twice in the opening 13 minutes to beat Sporting Lisbon 2-0 at home.
Their marksmen were Senegal's Amara Traore, after five minutes, and Didier Lang.

Another side to make an electrifying start were Ferencvaros of Hungary. They raced into a 2-0 lead over Newcastle after only 17 minutes with goals from Ferenc Horvath, who took advantage of an error by goalkeeper Pavel Srnicek after seven minutes, and Krisztian Lisztes.
The English league leaders fought back with a header from Les Ferdinand after 25 minutes and a stunning volley from his England strike partner Alan Shearer after 35 minutes.
But Lisztes scored his second midway through the second half to give Ferencvaros a surprise 3-2 win.
Valencia, who knocked holders Bayern Munich out in the last round, scored another impressive victory, winning 1-0 at Slavia Prague thanks to a Carlos Moya goal after 73 minutes.
The only blemish for Valencia was the sending-off of Jose Ignacio Saenz four minutes from time.
But their Spanish rivals Espanyol had a miserable night at home, losing 3-0 to Feyenoord who won with goals from Jean-Paul Van Gastel, Gaston Taument and Swede Henrik Larsson.
Italian club Inter Milan, looking to win the UEFA Cup for the third time in seven seasons, were indebted to an 81st minute goal by Frenchman Jocelyn Angloma for their 1-0 win over Casino Graz.
He appeared to strain a muscle as he celebrated his strike, the injury forcing him out of the match.
